design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (income_eligible_move_transfers, category access). Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [6, 6, 6, 6]; each of the four problems takes 6 factors.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The customer asks only to have her income-eligible share moved to her new National Grid apartment (root problem access_ext_move_reassignment_sizing). The reassignment is filed only after the subscription carries a move settlement payment received on or after her stated move-out date (state gate), the settlement is fixed only after every reversal carries its correction and every statement month 45 days past its end carries an estimate (two value inputs). The agent must discover, from published rules and the ledger, that (a) August 2026 has no posted credit 54 days after its end, (b) the utility partly reversed the July statement on 2026-10-13, (c) a settlement payment is owed by the household itself through the secure portal, and only then (d) size the kept share from the household's consumption record, which lives on the converted residential plan (another difficulty's records) because the Access share has no true-up of its own and the new account has no usage history. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling a ledger with mixed savings rates (plan 20 vs lapsed 10 after the overdue recertification), a partial reversal with a restated rate, two September postings (one priced, one not yet invoiced), and a cross-line true-up; never from tool choice.

2. SCOPE. Task 0 claims access_ext_move_reassignment_sizing (root, tool file_move_reassignment_5a7d54a1, agent), access_ext_move_settlement_payment (pay_move_settlement_0f5b0288, owner=user), access_ext_move_pending_estimate (bill_pending_estimate_ff226895), access_ext_move_partial_reversal_credit (credit_partial_reversal_7609dc6e). Task 1 claims the closed-share counterparts (closing payment, closing estimate, closed-share reversal credit) with disjoint tools. No (target_tool, computes) pair or policy is shared.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Edges: (E1) A0 <- P0, state_gate, gate access_billing.bill_date, form state, sentence "The reassignment of the share to the new account is filed only after the subscription carries a move settlement payment received on or after the move-out date the household stated."; condition: an access_payment_received line with bill_date on or after move_out_date 2026-09-26; resolver pay_move_settlement_0f5b0288 (owner user). False at opening: the latest payments are initial_state.access_billing.<pay1>.bill_date = 2026-08-01 and initial_state.access_billing.<pay2>.bill_date = 2026-08-20, both before 2026-09-26. Only the household's settlement payment writes a payment line in this difficulty, so the state singles out one write. (E2) P0 <- R0, value_input, gate credits_total, form state, sentence "The move settlement is fixed only after every reversal line posted on the subscription carries its reversal-correction billing credit."; false at opening: initial_state.access_credits.<rev07> exists and no access_billing line carries credit_reason credit_reversal_correction; resolver credit_partial_reversal_7609dc6e; skipping it moves the settlement from 111.50 to 145.78 (credits_total 34.28 -> 0). (E3) P0 <- E0, value_input, gate estimate_open, form state, negated direction "The move settlement is not fixed until every statement month that has gone the plan's estimate waiting period after its end without a posted credit carries an estimated charge."; false at opening: no access_credits line for statement_month 2026-08 and no estimated charge; resolver bill_pending_estimate_ff226895; skipping it moves the settlement from 111.50 to 105.13 (open-estimate share 23.29 -> 0 and the final-month prepayment basis 46.58 -> latest actual 42.57). Topological order: E0, R0 (either order), P0, A0. value_input edges 2 of 3 (>= max(3-1,1)). Four-point test per sentence: ordering connective (only after / not until), record-visible state (payment line date; billing credit per reversal; estimated charge per month), no tool, id or code token, scope exactly the edge's condition. The two directions differ by business habit: a filing is "filed only after", a settlement "is fixed only after" its corrections and "not fixed until" its estimates.

4. FACTOR CARD (tier taken, evidence, baseline figure from the sensitivity run).
A0 access_ext_move_reassignment_sizing (kW kept = 3.6; all-baseline 5.0): record_source (method, cross home, multi-source) — no access_reviews line AND the residential plan on the same old account (initial_state.home_subscriptions.<home>, closure_reason converted_to_access) carries initial_state.home_reviews.<review> (usage_kwh_12m 5000, credited_kwh_12m 5550, contract_kw 5.00 => record yield 1110) -> residential record; baseline (own true-up, none) moves the whole share: 5.0. banking_cap (parameter) — three access_credit_posted lines of the last twelve months carry banked value (July 6.10, both September postings) -> 90; baseline sizing_cap_pct 100 -> 4.0. verification_age_allowance (parameter) — income_verified_date 2024-06-07 is 865 days old (> 730) -> 97; baseline 100 -> 3.7. share_size_allowance (parameter) — initial filing 5.00 kW (3-6 kW band) -> 98; baseline 100 -> 3.7. restatement_allowance (parameter) — reversal posted 2026-10-13, 0 whole months ago -> 98; baseline 100 -> 3.7. conversion_allowance (parameter, cross home) — residential plan closed 2026-06-01, 4 whole months ago -> 97; baseline 100 -> 3.7. Supported share 90% x 5000 x .97 x .98 x .98 x .97 / 100 / 1110 = 3.6634 -> rounded down to 0.1 kW: 3.6; never above allocation_kw 5.00.
P0 access_ext_move_settlement_payment (111.50; all-baseline 0.00): standard = past-due figure 147.92 due - 118.54 paid - 34.28 credits = -4.90 (credit balance). not_yet_due_share — moved out 24 days ago (> 14) -> 100% of the not-yet-due September charge 42.57; baseline none -> 68.93. open_estimate_share — exactly one actual charge invoiced in the last two whole months (the 2026-10-17 September charge) -> 50% of the open estimate 46.58; baseline none -> 88.21. unbilled_statement_share — request received 14 days ago (> 7) -> 100% of the unbilled September supplement; baseline none -> 107.54. unbilled_banked_value (method) — supplement 8.80 wholly banked -> valued 4.40, priced at the rate in force 10 -> 3.96; baseline whole value 8.80 -> 115.46. final_month_prepay_share — latest payment 61 days ago (> 30) -> 100%; baseline none -> 64.92. final_month_prepay_basis (method) — an open estimated charge exists -> 46.58; baseline latest actual 42.57 -> 107.49.
E0 access_ext_move_pending_estimate (46.58; all-baseline 63.50): basis_rate_restatement (method) — billed basis 190.49 differs from the priced statements (229.98 less the unpriced latest 8.80 = 221.18) at the rate in force 10 (199.062) by more than one cent per charge, no billing-error credit -> restated 199.062; baseline billed 190.49 -> 44.18. reversal_deduction (method) — July reversal, single July posting -> 36.00 x 0.90 = 32.40 off; baseline nothing -> 55.63. young_share_pct — activation 2026-07-09, 3 whole months -> 90; baseline 100 -> 51.75. request_wait_pct — request 14 days old -> 97; baseline 100 -> 48.02. moved_out_pct — 24 days since move-out -> 98; baseline 100 -> 47.53. share_band_pct — initial 5.00 kW -> 98; baseline 100 -> 47.53. Average (199.062 - 32.40) / 3 = 55.554 x .90 x .97 x .98 x .98 = 46.58.
R0 access_ext_move_partial_reversal_credit (34.28; all-baseline 28.90; the reversed part is every reversal naming the July line): reversed_part_rate — the July line posted 2026-08-10, 64 days after recert_due_date 2026-06-07 (> 60) and income_verified_date 2024-06-07 not later -> lapsed 10; baseline plan 20 -> 30.47. corrected_value_basis (method) — reversal 36.00/300 kWh = 0.1200 per kWh vs line 88.20/700 = 0.1260 (gap 0.006 > 0.0005) -> 300 x 0.126 = 37.80; baseline 36.00 -> 32.64. held_interest_rate — 45 days from the due date 2026-09-05 -> 4.0; baseline 2.0 -> 34.19. held_days_start (method) — the check payment 2026-08-20 was received on or before the due date -> days from the due date (45); baseline days from the payment (61) -> 34.37. interest_year — paid by check -> 360-day year; baseline 365 -> 34.27. restatement_lag_uplift — reversal 64 days after the line posted -> +2.0; baseline 0 -> 34.19. 37.80 x 0.90 = 34.02 + 34.02 x 6% x 45/360 = 0.255 -> 34.28.
Near-miss records: the September supplement (2026-10-16) is the latest posting but unpriced, so the estimate basis leaves it out and the settlement prices it separately; the June charge was billed at the plan rate because its credit posted inside the recertification grace (DAYS(2026-06-07, 2026-07-09) = 32); the residential plan's 2026-05 statement exists but A0 reads its true-up, not its statements. Realism tags: banking_cap, verification/share-size/restatement/conversion allowances, the estimate percentages, the settlement shares and the interest schedule are Meadowlark's own published schedules (R6, keyed on recorded fields, at or below the program cap); record_source and the rate/value/reversal rules restate in-force base conventions.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. A0 writes access_allocation_reassigned (plus the same-filing move_resize line): governing base access_transfer_at_move (gates scoped to access_transfer_requested/completed, so policy_scope here): new account active, data_authorization_date 2026-10-06, same utility NATIONAL_GRID_NY as the project, request received 2026-10-06 = 10 days after the stated move-out (window 90 days, counted from the day after; the last window day 2026-12-25 still qualifies; 2026-12-26 would fail); income_documentation track follows the household. Filing calendar (NY_VDER monthly, cutoff 15): received 2026-10-06 <= 15 -> filed in 2026-10, effective 2026-11-01. P0 writes access_payment_received: access_evt_payment_application (policy_scope; secure portal, ach or card, no card numbers taken). E0 writes access_charge_billed: access_evt_subscription_charge gates one_charge_per_credit (the estimate prices no credit line: access_credit_id empty) and billable_status (transfer_pending is billable); access_recertification and access_benefit_basis (policy_scope; the estimate is priced only by the plan's own rate in force). Estimate trigger: August ended 2026-08-31, + 45 days = 2026-10-15 <= 2026-10-20; max one estimate in a row (none before). R0 writes access_billing_credited: access_evt_credit_correction gate one_correction_per_reversal (no correction exists for rev07); access_benefit_basis policy_scope.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Subscription <acc_sub> on old account 23-48120-77351; the offset charge is <ch07> (refers to credit <cr07>), the reversal <rev07> names <cr07>; the estimate is for 2026-08 (no credit line); the settlement pays the subscription's own ledger only; the reassignment carries request <acc_req_move> and moves the kept kW to the new account 23-48120-90418; the move_resize line removes 1.40 kW from the old account in the same filing.

7. SEED (why each row exists). Customer, two utility accounts (old final_billed 2026-09-30, new active with empty usage), NY project. Residential plan (Standard 10) from signing 2024-04-22 to conversion 2026-06-01 with 24 statements, charges at 10% and on-time ach payments (no late fee owed), its two allocation lines and its year-1 true-up (period 2024-07..2025-06, credited 5550 kWh, usage 5000; expected 5.0 x 1150 = 5750 does not exceed 115% of 5000, so no_change). Access 20 from signing 2026-04-27 (approved 2026-05-01, after the 3-business-day rescission), initial filing 2026-05 effective 2026-06-01, activation 2026-07-09; recert_due_date 2026-06-07 passed without recertification, so credits posted after 2026-08-06 are priced at the lapsed rate (July 79.38, September 42.57) while June (68.54) kept the plan rate. Payments 68.54 (ach) and 50.00 (check). Removing the reversal row removes R0's object and E0's deduction; removing the residential review sends A0 to the whole share.

8. PERSONA. Volunteered: she moved, sent the form, wants the share moved today. Given when asked: name, phone, date of birth, move-out date, new account number. Passive: pays herself by card when the payment is handed over; accepts a smaller share; acknowledges an estimate, a July credit or an overdue recertification without asking further. No prerequisite is named; no ask outside the tree.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify; read subscription, request, accounts, project, credits, billing, allocations, Access reviews (none), the residential plan with its filings, statements, settled ledger and true-up; bill the August estimate 46.58 due 2026-11-10; post the July reversal correction 34.28; hand over the settlement payment of 111.50 (card); file 3.6 kW to the new account in 2026-10, effective 2026-11-01 (move_resize 1.4 kW). Verification: scratch harness replays the tools and evaluates every compute at handling time; check_compute recomputes the same figures.

10. ORDER UNIQUENESS. The estimate and the reversal correction write different lines and neither compute reads the other's line (the estimate reads billing-error credits only and the reversal row, never the correction credit), so both orders give the same terminal state; the settlement reads both, the reassignment reads neither.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Villanueva, a home health aide in Syracuse who speaks quickly and a little impatiently because you are calling on your lunch break. On September 26 you moved out of your apartment at 3318 James Street, Apt 2, into a smaller apartment at 3352 Burnet Avenue, Apt 1R, still with National Grid, and earlier this month you filled in Meadowlark's online form to take your income-eligible solar share with you. You open the call by saying, in your own words, that you moved, that you already sent the form, and that you want your solar share moved to your new apartment today, done on this call rather than "in process" again.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your full name, Marisol Villanueva, and your phone number, 6515550141; if a second detail is needed you give your date of birth, 1981-09-14 (September 14, 1981). You do not know any Meadowlark reference numbers. If asked about the move, you say you moved out on September 26 and that the new National Grid account is in your name at 3352 Burnet Avenue, Apt 1R; you have the new account number on your welcome letter, 23-48120-90418, and you read it out only if the agent asks for it. You do not know how much electricity you used, how big your share is or what your credits were.
If the agent tells you that something has to be paid on your account before the share can be moved, you say that is fine and that you will pay it yourself right now with your debit card through the payment link; once the agent hands the payment over to you, you pay exactly the amount the agent gives you, by card, and you read back the receipt reference if the agent asks for it.
If the agent explains that the share at the new apartment will be smaller than the old one because of how much electricity your household used, you say that makes sense since the new place is smaller, and you accept it. If the agent mentions an estimated bill for a month, a credit for your July statement, or that your income paperwork is overdue for renewal, you say you understand and you do not ask anything further about it. You never ask for a refund, a discount or a different person.
Once the agent tells you the share has been filed to your new account and when it takes effect, you thank them and say goodbye.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write is keyed on the customer reference this lookup returns.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: No account detail may be discussed or written before identity is verified.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the move_transfer request: received_date 2026-10-06, stated move_out_date, new account, outcome received.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the old and new National Grid accounts: the new account is active, data-authorized, same utility, with no twelve months of usage on file (usage_as_of_month empty).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the project's program (NY_VDER) for the filing calendar (monthly, cutoff day 15).

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The estimate (bill_pending_estimate) and the reversal correction (credit_partial_reversal) write different ledger lines; the estimate's compute reads only billing-error credits and the reversal row, never the correction credit, and the correction's compute never reads the estimate. Replaying estimate-then-correction and correction-then-estimate gives the same two lines and the same settlement; the settlement reads both; the reassignment sizing reads neither (it reads reviews, credits, allocations, requests and the residential plan).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the settlement payment no payment line is dated on or after 2026-09-26, so the state gate stays false and the reassignment may not be filed; the terminal DB then lacks the 111.5 payment line (state_gate).
Skipping the reversal correction moves the settlement from 111.5 to 145.78 (credits_total 34.28 -> 0.00).
Skipping the estimate moves the settlement from 111.5 to 105.13 (open estimate 46.58 -> 0.00 and the final-month prepayment basis -> the latest actual charge 42.57).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario names no prerequisite: it never mentions an estimate, a reversal, a correction or a settlement before the agent does; the payment appears only as a conditional reaction ('If the agent tells you that something has to be paid on your account before the share can be moved ...'), and the estimate/credit mentions are passive acknowledgements after the agent raises them.
